description:
Bracket access on a keyword list ABORTS the process on every door.

  opts = [timeout: 30, retries: 2]
  opts[:timeout]

  fz run/interp/build:
    panicked at runtime/src/ir_runtime.rs:1654:
    fz_struct_get_named_field_ref: ExpectedTag { expected: ValueKind(3), found: ValueKind(1) }
    fatal runtime error: failed to initiate panic, error 5, aborting
  Elixir: 30   (and nil for a missing key)

`lhs[key]` is parsed as `Access.get/2` (frontdoor.rs bracket-access rule) and
decoded back into `Expr::Index` (quoted_function.rs is_access_get). `Expr::Index`
assumes a map or struct receiver and reaches a struct field read with a LIST
tag, which is not a diagnostic -- it is a non-unwinding abort.

Elixir's `Access` works on keyword lists as well as maps, and `opts[:key]` over
a keyword list is one of the most common shapes in real Elixir code.

MATTERS FOR THIS EPIC: fz-5xp.13 adds `Keyword`, whose entire surface is
keyword lists, and `keyword()` is already a declared type in runtime.fz. Any
`Keyword` code a user writes will reach for `opts[:key]`.

Pre-existing -- unrelated to fz-5xp.4, which only stopped `Alias.get/2` being
mistaken for an index. Found while writing that ticket's fixture, which
originally covered keyword bracket access and had to be narrowed.

FIX SHAPE: `Expr::Index` needs to dispatch on the receiver -- map/struct as
today, keyword list by key lookup, and anything else a clean diagnostic rather
than a struct read on a mistagged value.
title: Bracket access on a keyword list aborts the process
